load.name: Load images
load.desc: Pick the folder where your telescope or camera saved the images. Light, dark and flat frames are sorted automatically. You can also pick a single, already stacked image.

stack.name: Stack images
stack.desc: Many short exposures are combined into one much cleaner image. The frames are aligned precisely on the stars; dark and flat frames remove the sensor's own flaws.

align.label: Align images on the stars
align.help: Turn off if the images already line up exactly (e.g. an already stacked image).

reject.label: Skip poor frames automatically
reject.help: Frames that moved, were clouded out or show too few stars are left out.

gradient.label: Remove background gradient per frame
gradient.help: Under light-polluted skies the gradient shifts during the night; removing it per frame gives a cleaner average.

framing.label: Keep the full field of view
framing.help: Rotated frames can leave darker corners – crop them in the next step. When off, the result is cut to the reference frame.

clip.label: Filter outliers (satellite trails, hot pixels)
clip.help: Averages in two passes: the second pass drops values far from the mean. Slower but cleaner.

crop.name: Crop
crop.desc: Drag a rectangle over the part of the image you want to keep. If you select nothing, the thin faulty band left by stacking at the edges is removed.

margin.label: Trim edges
margin.help: The slider sets the selection shown on the image; you can fine-tune its edges with the mouse afterwards.

bge.name: Flatten background
bge.desc: Light pollution and the Moon leave an uneven, blotchy background. Here it is smoothed out so the sky is equally dark everywhere.

method.label: Method
method.help: The AI model recognises nebulae and galaxies and removes only the true background. The polynomial is simpler but needs a careful setting when a large object fills the frame.

model.label: AI model
model.help: Leave empty to use the newest model available.

smoothing.label: Smoothing
smoothing.help: Fine: the model follows smaller blotches too. Coarse: only the large, slow gradient is removed.

strength.label: Flattening strength (polynomial)
strength.help: Polynomial method only: how bright an area may be and still count as background.

correction.label: Correction
correction.help: Subtraction fixes light-pollution gradients; division fixes vignetting (darker corners).

deconv.name: Sharpen
deconv.desc: The atmosphere and the optics blur the details slightly. Sharpening reverses that as far as possible. Stars are tightened first, then the detail of nebulae and galaxies is brought out – each with its own AI model.

stars.label: Sharpen stars
stars.help: Stars become smaller and more point-like.

object.label: Sharpen nebula, galaxy
object.help: Fine structure (dust lanes, spiral arms) becomes more defined.

objectStrength.label: Nebula, galaxy – strength
objectStrength.help: Too much also amplifies noise – if it turns grainy, back off.

starsModel.label: AI model (stars)
starsModel.help: Leave empty to use the newest model available.

objectModel.label: AI model (nebula, galaxy)
objectModel.help: Leave empty to use the newest model available.

autoPsf.label: Measure star size automatically
autoPsf.help: The model needs to know how large the stars are (FWHM). When off, set it with the slider.

denoise.name: Reduce noise
denoise.desc: Long exposures and high ISO make the image grainy. Here it is smoothed while keeping the details.

platesolve.name: Identify the sky
platesolve.desc: From the star pattern we work out exactly where the image points. Needed for accurate colour calibration.

colorcal.name: Calibrate colours
colorcal.desc: Colours are matched to the known colours of the stars so nebulae look true to life.

starremoval.name: Separate stars
starremoval.desc: The stars are moved to a separate image temporarily, so nebula and stars can be treated each in its own way.

ghs.name: Bring out nebulae and galaxies
ghs.desc: The raw image is almost black: the faint detail hides in the dark. Here it is brought out without burning out the bright parts.

focus.label: Emphasis
focus.help: Where the contrast boost should be largest: the faintest nebulosity or the brighter core.

starstretch.name: Stretch stars
starstretch.desc: The stars are brightened separately and more gently so they stay small and colourful instead of white blobs.

recombine.name: Put stars back
recombine.desc: The separately enhanced nebula and the separately stretched stars are combined again.

green.name: Remove green cast
green.desc: There are no green nebulae in space – if your image looks greenish, that is the sensor. It is removed here; other colours stay untouched.

fringe.name: Fix colour fringes
fringe.desc: Bright stars may show a purple or blue fringe caused by the optics. Here it is faded out.

contrast.name: Contrast
contrast.desc: Slightly deeper darks, slightly livelier lights – the image "comes together". Careful: too much contrast swallows faint nebulosity.

saturation.name: Saturation
saturation.desc: The reds and blues of the nebulae and the colours of the stars become a little more vivid. Brightness is unchanged.

save.name: Save
save.desc: Your image is ready! Choose what you want to use it for; we set the rest.

welcome.title: Welcome to ClearStar!
welcome.lead: From raw frames to a finished astrophoto in three moves. We hold your hand all the way and explain what happens at every step.
welcome.s1sub: One folder is enough; we handle the rest.
welcome.s3sub: For sharing, printing or further editing.

about.title: About
about.tagline: Beginner-friendly astrophoto processing – from raw frames to the finished photo, step by step.
about.languageNote: The language change takes effect when the program restarts. New language: copy an xx.json file to:
about.gpu: Run AI models on the graphics card (DirectML)
about.gpuNote: When on, sharpening and background extraction are many times faster on any DirectX 12 graphics card (NVIDIA, AMD, Intel). If it causes trouble, turn it off – the CPU works too, just slower.
about.summary: ClearStar is the author's own work; the code is free to use, modify and redistribute under the GNU GPL 3.0 (or later). The stacking, stretching and background-extraction methods were written after studying the source code of Siril and GraXpert (both GPL-3.0) – no code was copied. The AI steps use the GraXpert Development Team's models, licensed CC BY-NC-SA 4.0: they may be used for non-commercial purposes only and are not included in ClearStar. The images you create with the program are yours. The program sends no data anywhere; the network is used only for model downloads you request. Details and the list of contributors are on the other tabs.
